author: Josie Heart
title: Stockton Police surprise families with 26th annual toy giveaway - NewsBreak
text:
By Josie Heart ,
2 hours ago
(FOX40.COM) — Christmas came bright and early for dozens of families across Stockton on Christmas Eve, with presents delivered not by sleigh, but by sirens.
The Stockton Police Department led its 26th annual toy giveaway Tuesday morning, surprising neighborhoods throughout the city by delivering toys, bicycles, and holiday cheer directly to families’ doorsteps.
On a rainy Christmas Eve morning, police sirens echoed through several quiet neighborhoods as officers arrived to deliver laughter, joy, and gifts by the truckload.
“We went to our first home, and as I knew it would be, it was very emotional. The family, extremely happy to see us,” said Stockton Police Chief Stanley McFadden.
Dozens of officers and volunteers from local agencies formed a caravan, winding through the city and stopping at multiple locations.
“The game plan is we have two teams, we’re going to hit 28 homes. We’re going to go to multiple hospitals and connect with another 30 children, and also hit some family centers as well,” said McFadden.
Trucks and trailers arrived with gifts collected through months of planning and donations. The generosity didn’t stop at the just the families on the list, as all children and families in the neighborhood were encouraged to participate and receive gifts.
While many of the stops were filled with surprises, others were deeply emotional. Some of the homes visited belong to families impacted by violence, tragedy, and loss.
“That’s where I get my hats off to my detectives, because not only are they working these very extensive investigative cases, they’re also connecting with these families,” said McFadden. “So, at this time of the year, they’re saying, hey, here are some homes that we should reach out to during the holiday season because they’ve had a tough year and we’re happy to be able to do that.”
Volunteers began gathering as early as 6 a.m., undeterred by the cold and rain.
“They see our faces, our laughter, our joking around. And they take part in that and almost becomes an instant block party,” said McFadden. “And everyone comes out and they start dispersing toys, cookies, dinner.”
For the chief and officers who have seen some of the city’s hardest moments, this morning was about something simple: bringing joy, relief, and a sense of community to all.
“Merry Christmas to everyone,” said McFadden. “Thank you for allowing me to serve you. Next year is going to be a great year, and I look forward to seeing you all.”
